uncited: Mark Invisible Cells is a preprocessing method used in voxel grid optimization to identify and mark voxels that are not visible to any training camera.
It sets the occupancy value of these invisible cells to -1, effectively excluding them from the training process.
This method is executed once before training begins.
It differs from sibling methods like [Occupancy Voxel Creation](2628-occupancy-voxel-creation.md) by focusing on visibility culling rather than density-based block detection.
The method determines visibility by projecting voxel centers into the camera space of all training views.
A voxel is considered visible if it projects within the image bounds and lies in front of the near plane for at least one camera.
- `self.aabbs`: Axis-aligned bounding boxes for each level, shape $(L, 6)$, where $L$ is the number of levels. `aabbs[lvl, :3]` is the minimum corner, `aabbs[lvl, 3:]` is the maximum corner.
- Assert `K.dim() == 3` and `K.shape[1:] == (3, 3)`.
- Assert `c2w.dim() == 3` and `(c2w.shape[1:] == (3, 4) or c2w.shape[1:] == (4, 4))`.
- Assert `K.shape[0] == c2w.shape[0]` or `K.shape[0] == 1`.
- `w2c_R = c2w[:, :3, :3].transpose(2, 1)` with shape $(N, 3, 3)$.
Get all cell indices across levels: `lvl_indices = self._get_all_cells()`.
Retrieve voxel coordinates: `grid_coords = self.grid_coords[indices]`.
- Extract chunk coordinates: `x = grid_coords[i : i + chunk] / (self.resolution - 1)`.
- Extract chunk indices: `indices_chunk = indices[i : i + chunk]`.
- Precision issues in UV normalization when depth is very small.
- Boundary conditions for image width/height.
- Degenerate input where `K` or `c2w` shapes are incorrect.
- **Time Complexity:** $O(N \cdot C)$, where $N$ is the number of cameras and $C$ is the number of cells.
- **Memory Complexity:** $O(N \cdot C)$ for intermediate tensors.
Does not account for occlusions within the scene.
Mark Invisible Cells is part of the voxel grid optimization pipeline in neural radiance fields.
It helps in reducing the computational load by ignoring voxels that do not contribute to the rendered images.
